name: Justin Welby
role: Archbishop of Canterbury (2013–2025); former oil executive
summary: Welby grounds public policy in Christian solidarity, supporting social protection, unions, refugee responsibilities and climate action. His later support for same-sex blessings coexists with continuing distinctions around marriage.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Insists that everyone receive high-quality medical care free at delivery.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Demands genuine living wages sufficient for ordinary household needs.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Personally advocated taxing wealth more when launching economic reform proposals.

unions-good.rationale: Calls for renewed unionisation wherever vulnerable workers lack protection.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Condemns insecure contracts and corporate tax avoidance; demands protective reform.

cut-welfare.rationale: Condemns austerity for crushing vulnerable people and weakening essential services.

decide-locally.rationale: Endorses subsidiarity: decisions at the lowest feasible institutional level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prisons should offer treatment, reconciliation and rehabilitation alongside accountability.

traditional-family.rationale: Earlier defended traditional marriage as foundational; later embraces stable same-sex households while retaining marriage distinctions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Opposed civil legislation, accepted its legitimacy, and later supported blessings; church marriage remains distinct.

more-religion-public.rationale: Proposes Christian virtues as foundations for shared public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Defends targeted investment addressing slavery’s continuing effects and dehumanising attitudes.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wants inherited virtues retained and adapted to contemporary diversity.

gradual-change.rationale: Advocates progressive change embedded in virtues and traditions rather than sharp turns.

nation-first.rationale: Britain should share international refugee responsibilities rather than outsource them.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Accepts military hard power contributing to the necessary enforcement of peace.

open-borders.rationale: Calls for effective immigration controls and agreed limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Demands bolder government climate action and a just fossil-fuel transition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Praises Elizabeth II’s contribution as a queen beneficial to country and world.

democracy-best.rationale: Accepts the referendum defeat and rejects overturning it despite favouring Remain.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Affirms inherent worth in land, livestock and crops themselves.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejects frozen traditions and nostalgic idealisation of family life.

taxation-theft.rationale: Paying a fair community tax contribution is a moral obligation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Explicitly defends the Palestinian people’s fundamental self-determination right.

class-collaboration.rationale: Government, unions, churches, businesses and communities must act in partnership.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Calls for the fossil-fuel era to end through a fair transition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Welcoming newcomers should change and enrich the receiving culture too.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Requires public healthcare and properly funded education beyond basic protective functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Affirms every person’s equal dignity as made in God’s image.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Calls for religious education even for pupils who do not believe.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Celebrates ethnic and religious diversity through integration without conformity.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Favoured EU membership for greater European contribution to the world; accepted Brexit.

death-penalty.rationale: Explicitly opposes capital punishment for any offence.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Celebrates Britain’s substantial aid commitment as international solidarity.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Demands an end to unlawful Israeli occupation and settlement annexation.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: International human-rights safeguards must constrain even elected governments.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade deals must protect environmental and animal-welfare standards, not export harm.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Affirms Parliament’s sovereign right to decide church establishment.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Supports farming with high animal-welfare standards and respect for livestock.

non-intervention.rationale: Supports external assistance to Ukraine and military contributions to peacemaking.

local-production.rationale: Urges eating locally and seasonally, including British food in schools.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Defends international law’s role in constraining domestic government action.

religious-nation.rationale: Describes Britain as having Christian heritage, carefully avoiding defining it as Christian.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Strongly rejects criminalisation of gay and lesbian people.

assisted-dying.rationale: Opposes legalisation as dangerous and liable to expand beyond its safeguards.

social-market-economy.rationale: Welcomes properly disciplined markets alongside universal care and social solidarity.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Values British military capabilities as part of effective peacebuilding.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Describes changing his understanding through study and experience of faithful same-sex relationships.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Seeks safer, rehabilitative prisons while retaining criminal accountability.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Affirms all orders of ministry equally open regardless of gender.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Wants Britain to join the treaty prohibiting nuclear weapons.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Supports Ukraine’s armed defence against invasion.

god-not-male.rationale: Rejects defining God as either male or female; human language is metaphorical.

second-chamber.rationale: Defends the Lords’ revising function and independent legislative scrutiny.

family-wage.rationale: Wages should prevent routine household replacement costs becoming family crises.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Public flourishing requires spiritual virtues beyond material prosperity.

future-generations.rationale: Climate obligations extend our covenant to generations not yet born.

arms-reduction.rationale: Supports abolishing nuclear weapons, without calling for abolition of conventional forces.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions should negotiate technological change and secure adequate living wages.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Signed a call for Britain to join the nuclear prohibition treaty.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Integration needs English learning for mutual communication.

premarital-sex.rationale: His evolved position accepts sexual intimacy in faithful committed relationships without requiring marriage.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Promotes new technology through inherited community values and sustainable innovation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says racist mindsets still blight millions of African-descended people’s lives.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Says Christian conscience can require refusing what the law demands.

notes: Personal views are distinguished from church-wide positions and ceremonial duties. Later sexuality statements supersede earlier blanket opposition to intimacy, but do not clearly endorse every form of marriage. The IPPR report explicitly disclaims individual endorsement of each recommendation, so commission membership does not establish its specific proposals. Church investment responding to slavery does not establish state-to-state colonial reparations. Asylum criticism does not imply unrestricted immigration; peacemaking does not imply pacifism. General religious conviction does not establish a position on abortion law.
